The actual linear-tail regime supplies a genuine invariant coordinate and matches all hypotheses of the published nice-derivation recognition theorem. This is a sufficient criterion, not a claim that all tails can be made linear.

A uniform formal noninvertible family has first-tail degree and exact inverse-field degree n for every n>=2. Its relative Jacobian one does not repair its nonunit original Jacobian or failed polynomial return.

For any first-tail component on which Psi is transcendental over L, all later formal Taylor/cofactor recurrences persist automatically. Such a component is simple, but need not have a polynomial curve ring or the original inverse-field structure.

Thus searching for an additional formal recurrence alone cannot exclude a Psi-transcendental extra component. The next bridge must use actual source coefficient-field compatibility, polynomial return or inverse-field generation.
